subject: Clarify processor scope and SOC 2 coverage for UK hosting
messages:
From: Elena Fischer <elena.fischer@midlandsbank.co.uk>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: privacy-team@midlandsbank.co.uk
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00+00:00
Subject: SOC 2 / hosting scope question for UK deployment

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. As part of our procurement checklist, our privacy team needs clarity on two items before we progress to legal:

1) For customers who choose Redwood Private in our UK region, which components are in-scope as "processor" for the 2026 SOC 2 Type II report? Specifically: control plane only, control plane + data plane, or all hosted components?

2) Do you have a bridge letter or attestation that covers cross-border transfers (UK -> US) during the SOC 2 audit window if any transient logs or metrics are routed out-of-region for support/observability?

Can you point me to the SOC 2 report and any short-form language we can include in our supplier risk register? We have a legal review kickoff next Wednesday.

Best,
Elena
Elena Fischer
Head of Third-Party Risk
Midlands Bank

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Fischer <elena.fischer@midlandsbank.co.uk>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:03:00+00:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / hosting scope question for UK deployment

Hi Elena,

Thanks — great questions. Short answers up front:
- Redwood's 2026 SOC 2 Type II report covers the control plane and the managed hosted control-plane services for hosted customers; for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) customers, the SOC 2 coverage we can provide is limited to the customer-managed control plane components that Redwood operates (eg. private control plane APIs, key management connectors) — we do not assert coverage over customer-managed data plane storage unless Redwood is operating that component under a Dedicated/managed configuration.
- We can provide a bridge letter that clarifies our position on transient telemetry or support artifacts leaving the UK during an audit window; the letter can include mitigating controls and retention policies.

Im attaching the redacted SOC 2 Type II snapshot we share with prospects and a short network diagram of the UK hosting footprint. Will loop in our security lead to draft a bridge-letter template for your review.

Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_2026.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: redwood-hosting-network-diagram.png (png)

Next steps: Ill ask Mina to add the standard bridge wording and timeline (we aim to turn a draft in 48 business hours). If you need anything more formal (attestation language for contract exhibits), let me know and we can escalate to legal.

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Fischer <elena.fischer@midlandsbank.co.uk>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: privacy-team@midlandsbank.co.uk
Date: 2027-04-19T08:45:00+00:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / hosting scope question for UK deployment

Hi Elena — looping Marissa from Security & Compliance (commercial).

Quick clarifications to Sergio's note:
- For Dedicated deployments where Redwood provisions and operates both control and data plane within a UK region as part of the contract, those managed components are included in Redwood's SOC 2 scope (and will be explicitly enumerated).
- For Private (customer-managed VPC) where the customer controls data plane storage/network, Redwood's SOC 2 report covers only the Redwood-operated control plane services and the secure connectors we operate to integrate with customer infra.

Elena, to make legal's life easier weve attached a single-page summary you can paste into your supplier risk register that states the precise boundaries. Also attaching the network diagram and a draft bridge-letter (work-in-progress).

Attachment: supplier-scope-summary.txt (txt)
Attachment: bridge-letter-draft.docx (docx)

We're ready to produce a signed bridge letter once you confirm the audit window dates and whether Midlands Bank will require explicit wording around telemetry egress minimization and log retention thresholds.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Fischer <elena.fischer@midlandsbank.co.uk>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-19T14:05:00+00:00
Subject: Draft bridge letter and egress controls

Elena / team,

Please find below the proposed bridge letter excerpt and the key egress controls we recommend including. Ive kept the language concise so it can be included as an addendum to your supplier statement.

--- bridge letter excerpt ---
Redwood Inference confirms that for the audit period ending 2026-12-31, Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report covers the Redwood-operated control plane and any Dedicated-managed data plane components that are contractually operated within the UK region. For customers using Redwood Private (customer-managed VPC), Redwood's SOC 2 assertions are limited to the Redwood-operated control plane components and integrations. Redwood maintains telemetry minimization and retention controls; transient support artifacts may be routed outside of the UK for operational reasons but are subject to access controls, limited retention (max 90 days), and are logged for audit.
--- end excerpt ---

Key controls to cite:
- Telemetry minimization: only anonymized metadata collected for system health unless customer enables debug-mode.
- Retention: transient support logs retained no longer than 90 days; access logged and reviewed quarterly.
- Access controls: RBAC + just-in-time access for support engineers; requests require approval and are time-limited.

I can convert this into a signed PDF and include an exhibit describing the exact components in-scope by deployment type. If Midlands needs DPA language, we can also surface a short addendum.

Attachment: bridge-letter-draft.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Senior Security Manager, Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Fischer <elena.fischer@midlandsbank.co.uk>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-20T15:27:00+00:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 / hosting scope question for UK deployment

Thanks all — that helps a lot. A couple of follow-ups from our legal/tech risk: 

1) Please confirm the audit window covered by the attached SOC 2 PDF (we noted 2026 but need explicit start/end dates in text we can reference).
2) Can you produce the signed bridge letter as a PDF and include the exhibit mapping managed components (control plane vs data plane) with hostnames/regions redacted?

If you can get those to us by EOD Thursday our legal team will include the language in the supplier assessment and move us to contract redlines. Otherwise we may need a short one-week extension before legal will sign off.

Best,
Elena
